reply:
By default `git pull` runs `git fetch` followed by `git merge`. Rebase only happens if you pass `--rebase` or set `pull.rebase=true` in config.

I had it backwards. The merge strategy preserves history linearly (creates a merge commit), so it doesn't rewrite. Your teammate either ran `git pull --rebase`, has that config option set, or pulled into a state where fast-forward happened and they're misreading what occurred.

grade.note: Reply correctly adopts merge-by-default position and explains rebase requires --rebase or config.
